title: Beyond Next-Token Prediction: A Performance Characterization of Diffusion versus Autoregressive Language Models
gist: A theoretical-plus-profiling study of Diffusion Language Models against Autoregressive Language Models finds that DLMs win on arithmetic intensity through parallel token generation but fail to scale with long contexts, while ARMs keep superior throughput under batched inference. Block-wise decoding decouples DLM arithmetic intensity from sequence length, and cutting the number of sampling steps is identified as the key lever for open-source DLMs to beat ARM latency.

themes.theme: Sequential decoding as a hardware-efficiency ceiling

insights.claim: Autoregressive language models exhibit low arithmetic intensity because next-token prediction imposes an inherent sequential dependency, leaving modern accelerators underutilized during generation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Low arithmetic intensity is why LLM decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound rather than FLOP-bound — the structural reason inference hardware demand skews toward memory bandwidth and HBM rather than raw compute.
insights.quote: they exhibit low arithmetic intensity due to the inherent sequential dependency in next-token prediction
insights.locator: Abstract: 'While these models have achieved high accuracy'

insights.claim: Diffusion Language Models generate output tokens in parallel, which is the specific mechanism by which they escape the limits of sequential decoding.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Parallel token emission is the architectural claim behind the DLM investment thesis — worth verifying against the long-context caveat below before assuming it translates to production savings.
insights.locator: Abstract: 'DLMs generate output tokens in parallel'

insights.claim: The performance implications of Diffusion Language Models relative to commonly deployed autoregressive models were not fully understood, so this study pairs theoretical analysis with empirical profiling to characterize the trade-offs.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Signals that DLM-versus-ARM comparisons circulating before this work rested on architecture arguments rather than measured serving behavior — discount vendor claims made without profiling.
insights.quote: the performance implications of DLMs relative to commonly deployed ARMs are not fully understood
insights.locator: Abstract: 'However, the performance implications of DLMs'

insights.claim: Diffusion Language Models achieve higher arithmetic intensity than autoregressive models by exploiting parallelism across token positions, but they fail to scale effectively as context length grows.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The headline DLM efficiency advantage evaporates exactly in the long-context regime that agentic and document workloads live in — a direct check on claims that diffusion LMs are about to displace autoregressive serving.
insights.quote: although DLMs can achieve higher arithmetic intensity than ARMs by leveraging parallelism across token positions, they fail to scale effectively with longer contexts
insights.locator: Abstract: 'We show that although DLMs can achieve higher arithmetic intensity'

insights.claim: Block-wise decoding decouples a diffusion language model's arithmetic intensity from sequence length and restores long-context scaling behavior comparable to autoregressive models.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Block-wise decoding is the concrete engineering fix that would make DLMs deployable at long context — its adoption is the milestone to watch before treating diffusion LMs as a serving-cost threat to ARMs.
insights.quote: block-wise decoding for DLMs, which decouples arithmetic intensity from sequence length and enables better scaling to long contexts (similar to ARMs)
insights.locator: Abstract: 'We then explore block-wise decoding for DLMs'

insights.claim: Under batched inference, autoregressive models deliver superior throughput because they benefit more than diffusion models from parallelism across sequences in the batch.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Real serving is batched, so the DLM efficiency case is weakest in the deployment mode that actually matters for cost per query at a large inference provider.
insights.quote: ARMs exhibit superior throughput as they benefit more from parallelism across sequences in the batch

insights.claim: Reducing the number of sampling steps is identified as the decisive lever for open-source diffusion language models to achieve lower latency than autoregressive models.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Step-count reduction, not model size or hardware, is the metric that determines whether diffusion LMs become latency-competitive — track few-step distillation progress as the leading indicator.
insights.quote: reducing the number of sampling steps is key for open-source DLMs to achieve lower latency relative to ARMs
insights.locator: Abstract closing: 'Finally, we highlight opportunities for accelerating DLM inference'
